subject: Refactor map operations for improved configuration handling and template rendering
message:
Refactor map operations for improved configuration handling and template rendering

- Removed Flask dependency and related code from `map.py`.
- Introduced `render_jinja_template` function in `optimizers/utils.py` for secure Jinja2 template rendering.
- Updated `MapOperation` and `ParallelMapOperation` to use kwargs for initialization and configuration.
- Added `safe_eval` function in `utils.py` for secure expression evaluation using `asteval`.
- Modified `call_llm_with_validation` to accept a list of dictionaries for messages.
- Updated tests to reflect changes in `ParallelMapOperation` initialization and configuration.
- Added `batch_size` and `clustering_method` to `api.py` and `builder.py` for better configuration management.
- Removed Flask dependency from `pyproject.toml` and added `asteval`.

- Optimize `Makefile` to run tests in parallel using `pytest -n auto`.

subject: Add structured output mode support to pandas API (#394)
message:
Add structured output mode support to pandas API (#394)

* Add structured output mode support to pandas API

This commit addresses issue #393 by adding the ability to specify structured
output mode in the pandas semantic accessor.

Key changes:
- Enhanced map() method to accept 'output' parameter with schema and mode
- Added support for 'structured_output' mode alongside existing 'tools' mode
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing 'output_schema' parameter
- Added comprehensive parameter validation and error handling

New API format:
```python
df.semantic.map(
    prompt="Extract data: {{input.text}}",
    output={
        "schema": {"name": "str", "age": "int"},
        "mode": "structured_output"  # Optional, defaults to "tools"
    }
)
```

Tests added:
- test_semantic_map_structured_output: Tests new structured output functionality
- test_semantic_map_invalid_output_mode: Tests output mode validation
- test_semantic_map_structured_output_vs_tools: Compares both output modes
- test_semantic_map_backward_compatibility: Ensures old API still works
- test_semantic_map_parameter_validation: Comprehensive parameter validation

Interactive progress view for pipeline runs (terminal) (#488)

* docs: design proposal for interactive progress visualization (#487)

Adds a design doc proposing a structured telemetry foundation that feeds
both an interactive terminal TUI (Textual) and the web UI, addressing the
request for a full-screen, dot-grid progress view that scales to tens of
thousands of documents.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XB5w3mQu48VxBKWG5MxDKy

* docs: correct motivation framing for progress UI (#487)

Today's output isn't a scrolling wall of text — it's an in-place tqdm bar
per op plus summary panels. Reframe the goal as adding per-document
browsable visibility rather than replacing overwhelming output.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XB5w3mQu48VxBKWG5MxDKy

* docs: enable TUI via pipeline.interactive_ui YAML flag (#487)

Primary switch is a declarative config flag (pipeline.interactive_ui: true)
with a CLI --tui/--no-tui override, TTY-gated with fallback. Validated via
PipelineSpec in base_schemas.py.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XB5w3mQu48VxBKWG5MxDKy

* feat: interactive progress TUI for pipeline runs (#487)

Adds a structured progress telemetry layer and a full-screen Textual TUI
that visualizes a pipeline run as a three-pane dashboard: operations list,
a per-document dot grid (paged at moderate scale, heatmap at tens of
thousands of docs), and a document detail pane showing output + the prompt.

Foundation (surface-agnostic):
- docetl/progress: thread-safe ProgressTracker + RunState/OpState model.
- RichLoopBar.update() ticks the active tracker, so per-document progress
  works across every operation with no per-operation changes (the DAG runs
  one op at a time, so a single 'current op' is well-defined).
- containers.py emits op_start/op_done (incl. cost + per-op token deltas),
  and now surfaces cached operations as done so they aren't stuck 'queued'.

TUI (opt-in):
- Enabled via pipeline.interactive_ui: true in the YAML, with a CLI
  --tui/--no-tui override; TTY-gated with graceful fallback to plain output.
- textual moved to an optional [tui] extra; lazy import with install hint.

Tested: unit tests for the tracker/cell-status; a stubbed end-to-end run
through the real runner/operations (OpenAI host is blocked in this sandbox,
so the model call is faked) drives the live grid correctly.

* feat: operator coverage for the progress TUI (reduce/resolve/split/…) (#487)

Phase 2 of the progress-visualization plan: make the live view correct and
inspectable for every operator type, not just map/filter, and structure it as
a default UI with operator-specific overrides.

Progress units:
- RichLoopBar now reports its real unit count to the tracker via
  ProgressTracker.set_phase, so the denominator reflects what the op actually
  ticks — documents for map/filter, groups for reduce, comparisons for
  resolve/equijoin — instead of the raw input-doc count guessed in containers.

Operator profiles (docetl/tui/profiles.py):
- A small registry maps an op type to a unit word + optional per-document
  provenance / summary, all falling back to a default profile so unknown ops
  still render. Provenance is read from metadata the operators already emit
  (reduce's _counts_prereduce_* source counts; split's chunk_num/id, paired by
  prefix) — no global document-id system, as agreed.

Doc grid:
- OpState.grid_count shows one cell per work unit while running and switches to
  one cell per output document once finished, so fan-out (split) and fan-in
  (reduce/resolve) ops are both inspectable; cell_status renders a finished op's
  output cells as done regardless of the work-unit counter.

Efficiency: the detail pane caches each doc's serialized JSON (outputs are
immutable post-op_done) so it isn't re-dumped every 0.15s frame.

Tests + real screenshots (gpt-4.1-nano, ~$0.002 total):
- tests/test_tui_profiles.py: grid_count, done-state cell_status, and the

- tests/tui_operator_screenshots.py + tui_demo reduce/resolve/split pipelines;

invasive; documented in the design doc.

Address visual feedback on the progress view:

Tests updated for the new provenance signature / wording (15 passing).

(e.g. 2 vs 2), so the join returned 1 match instead of 2 even with retries.

* fix: TUI froze on a tqdm/multiprocessing crash; move interactive_ui to top level

Two fixes from real-world use:

1. The interactive view never updated and the run died immediately. tqdm builds
   a multiprocessing write-lock on first use, which spawns a helper process;
   under Textual's control of the terminal that fork_exec fails ("bad value(s)
   in fds_to_keep"), so the first operation's progress bar threw and the UI
   froze on a stale frame. Fixes:
   - run_with_tui pins tqdm to a plain thread lock before launching, so any bar
     created during the run is safe.
   - RichLoopBar skips tqdm entirely when the interactive tracker is active (the
     dashboard draws its own progress); the non-TUI path is unchanged.
   - The dashboard now shows the error text (not just "failed") when a run
     raises, so a failure is obvious instead of looking stuck.

2. interactive_ui is now a top-level config key (alongside default_model)
   instead of nested under `pipeline`. It was only read from pipeline.*, so a
   natural top-level `interactive_ui: true` was silently ignored and nothing
   launched. Moved the schema field to the root config and updated the docs.

* feat: show "?" when a stage's document count isn't known; exit prompt + summary

- The document grid is only drawn when we actually know a document count: the
  op has finished, or its live progress counts documents (map/filter/reduce/
  split). For resolve/equijoin (which count comparison batches, not documents)
  or any op whose total isn't known yet, the grid now shows a clear "?" with a
  one-line explanation instead of a tiny, misleading dot grid. The header shows
  "? docs" rather than a number in that case.
- Fix a stale-state bug where an op with no grid could leave a leftover
  "page 1/3" in the header from a previously selected operation.
- The detail pane falls back to the operation summary when there are no
  enumerable documents (instead of "Document #0 — not available").
- On completion the dashboard prompts "press q to exit", and after the TUI
  closes a short summary (cost + output path) is printed back in the terminal.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01GVbRRJKoKHapgdgnawLHsX

* docs: note that resolve/equijoin show ? while running (count not yet known)

* docs: refresh progress-view screenshots and video for the latest UI

Regenerated from real gpt-4.1-nano runs with the current rendering: single-
border panes, hollow to-do circles, live document streaming, and resolve's "?"
indicator (its grid can't enumerate documents while it counts comparisons).

* docs: tour individual documents (with reading pauses) in the progress video

* test: make equijoin test deterministic with an explicit blocking condition

Root cause of the recurring failure: with no blocking config, equijoin
auto-computes an embedding-similarity blocking threshold from a *random* sample
and landed on 1.0000; whether the true-match pairs (1↔1, 2↔2) clear a 1.0 cosine
threshold depends on embedding floating-point and the sample, so some runs
dropped a real match and returned 1 result instead of 2 (retries didn't help —
each run is internally consistent).

Add an exact-match blocking condition ("left['id'] == right['user_id']") — the
realistic config for an id join, matching the operator's own docstring example —
so blocking deterministically selects the matching pairs. Verified across
repeated cache-cleared runs.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01GVbRRJKoKHapgdgnawLHsX

* fix(equijoin,resolve): don't auto-block tiny inputs; never pick a 1.0 threshold

The auto-blocking optimizer estimates a similarity threshold from a small random
sample. On tiny inputs that sample is far too small (e.g. a 3x3 join samples ~2
pairs), so it picks an unstable threshold and can drop true matches — which made
test_equijoin_operation flaky (1 result instead of 2), and would silently
under-recall any small join/dedup.

- equijoin: when there's no blocking config and the join is small
  (len(left) * len(right) <= 100), compare all pairs instead of auto-blocking.
- resolve: only auto-compute a threshold when there are more than 10 items;
  otherwise fall through to the existing "compare all pairs" path.
- blocking optimizer: never select a threshold of exactly 1.0. Cosine similarity
  of a true match is rarely exactly 1.0 in floating point, so a 1.0 threshold
  drops real matches even when the sample reported full recall.
- test_equijoin_operation: drop the explicit blocking workaround so it exercises
  (and regression-tests) the small-join path. Verified deterministic across
  repeated cache-cleared runs.

Simplify MOAR interface and add Python API (#490)

Introduces a simplified Python interface for MOAR optimization that:
- Auto-detects available LLM providers from env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY,

subject: Model cascades: cut LLM cost on binary operators with statistical quality guarantees (#491)
message:
Model cascades: cut LLM cost on binary operators with statistical quality guarantees (#491)

* Add model-cascade engine with statistical guarantees (milestone 1)

Introduce a guarantee-bearing proxy/oracle cascade engine that can later
back filter, map-with-enum, resolve, and equijoin. CategoricalCascade runs
a cheap proxy on all items, learns a confidence threshold on an
oracle-labeled sample, and escalates the rest while guaranteeing a target
accuracy/precision/recall holds with probability 1-delta.

The statistical core (betting confidence sequences, without-replacement
adaptive sampling, threshold search) is a dependency-free reimplementation
of the BARGAIN procedures, adapted to pluggable proxy/oracle callables.

Includes a design doc and model-free statistical correctness tests
verifying guarantee coverage across many trials.

* Record vendoring decision and rationale in cascade design doc

* Add UserPromptSubmit hook for cascade milestone progress reports

Surfaces .claude/cascade-progress.md and reminds to report status against
the model-cascade plan each turn.

* Add classify_with_logprob proxy path for model cascades (milestone 2)

Single-token numeric-menu classification with softmax confidence over the
answer token's logprobs, plus a pure parser (_parse_logprob_response) and
model-free tests covering parsing, validation, and the completion call.

* Ignore generated cascade-report.html artifact

* Add filter model-cascade vertical slice (milestone 3)

Opt-in cascade: block on filter runs the engine over records via a proxy
(classify_with_logprob) and the existing oracle call, keeping records the
engine labels positive. Refactor classify_with_logprob to expose a
cost-returning internal so proxy cost is accounted without changing its
public (label, prob) contract. Adds 7 model-free filter tests (29 total).

* Generalize model cascade to map(enum), resolve, equijoin (milestone 4)

Extract shared CascadeConfig + CascadeMixin (cascade_runner.py); refactor
filter onto it. Add cascade branches:
- map: single-enum output, accuracy guarantee, all rows kept
- resolve/equijoin: _cascade_match_pairs over blocked candidate pairs,
  precision guarantee, feeding existing clustering/join (per-batch oracle
  loop emptied to no-op when cascade is on)
Each execute() branch is guarded so default behavior is unchanged. Adds 8
new model-free tests (37 total).

* Add cascade caching, cost/escalation reporting, and docs (milestone 5)

- Cache the cascade result in the shared DocETL cache, keyed on op identity +
  config + dataset signature; identical re-runs skip proxy/oracle calls.
  Honors bypass_cache.
- _report_cascade logs a cost/escalation summary and exposes op.cascade_stats.
- User docs at docs/concepts/cascades.md (+ mkdocs nav); design doc marked
  complete. Adds 4 caching/reporting tests (41 total).

* Guard cascade against unsupported inputs (pdf_url_key / retriever)

Reject combining cascade with pdf_url_key or a retriever at config
validation, since the cascade path renders text only and would otherwise
silently drop the PDF / retrieved context. Add an autouse fixture isolating
the cascade cache per test (the on-disk cache leaked across runs and broke
call-count assertions). +3 guard tests (44 total).

* docs: add runnable end-to-end cascade example + invocation and sample logs

* docs: clarify oracle/proxy call accounting, label_budget ceiling, and guarantee semantics

* Stop tracking session-local progress-report hook tooling

Untrack .claude/hooks/cascade-progress-report.sh and .claude/cascade-progress.md
(kept on disk for this session) and gitignore them; they are developer tooling,
not part of the model-cascade feature.

* Replace hand-ported cascade stats with bargain library + add cascade progress logging

The statistical core (betting confidence sequences, WoR sampler, threshold
searches) was a verbatim port of BARGAIN — now use the actual library via
thin adapter classes that bridge BARGAIN's Proxy/Oracle class API with
DocETL's callable-based pattern. Cuts ~470 lines.

Also pipes console into the cascade engine so users see progress during
execution: cascade start/params, proxy scoring, threshold search, and
escalation summary — previously the only log line appeared after completion.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2R9WU8NGd3bcszUaT3KAC

* better pritning

* Support embedding models as the cascade proxy

cascade.proxy_model can now name an embedding model (detected via
litellm's model registry — no new syntax). Instead of one cheap LLM call
per item, the cascade embeds every item in batches, oracle-labels a
training slice out of label_budget, fits a logistic-regression head on
those embeddings, and uses the head's probabilities as proxy scores.
The BARGAIN threshold search then runs unchanged on the remaining
budget, with disjoint labels so the statistical bounds stay valid.

Details:
- Training rows keep their oracle answers in the output and oracle
  calls are memoized, so threshold-search re-draws of training rows
  cost nothing — the budget split's only real cost is a slightly more
  conservative threshold.
- If the training slice comes back single-class the head can't be fit
  and everything escalates to the oracle (logged, graceful).
- A post-split budget warning fires when fewer than ~50 labels remain
  for a precision/recall search; docs recommend ~2x the LLM-proxy
  budget for embedding proxies.
- sklearn was already a dependency (cluster op); embeddings go through
  the cached, rate-limited gen_embedding path and show up in the token
  table as the cascade proxy.

Verified with fake-API unit tests (separability, no LLM proxy calls,
budget accounting, single-class fallback, cache reuse) and a real
end-to-end run (200 reviews, text-embedding-3-small proxy + gpt-4o-mini
oracle: recall 0.98 at target 0.9, $0.003 total).

subject: Typed relational logical plan IR (#497)
message:
Typed relational logical plan IR (#497)

* Add typed relational logical-plan IR with rewrite rules and MOAR validation

* Fix all 13 review findings: fail-closed trait analysis, honest cardinality, gated rewrites

A verified review of the plan-IR commit found that the rewrite rules
trust the operator traits absolutely while the traits were written
against op schemas instead of execute() semantics. Root-cause fixes:

Extractor soundness (every static→runtime value boundary fails closed):
- Jinja: input.get('x') reads 'x' (not phantom 'get'); input.items()/
  keys()/values() and dynamic .get keys return None
- Code: doc param identified via inspect.signature matched by name in
  the AST (bound methods kept 'self' positionally and returned ∅);
  multi-arg transforms return None; results cached
- map.fields_read covers validate expressions (evaluated against the
  passthrough-merged output dict) and resolves dotted pdf_url_key to
  its root field

Trait honesty:
- Cardinality.ONE_TO_ONE documented as an at-most contract (row-local
  drops allowed) — sufficient for selection swaps, not positional ones
- extract mirrors execute()'s skip_on_error=True default (not 1:1)
- unnest fields_written → None without expand_fields (dict unnest
  writes runtime keys)
- filter inherits map's fields_written/is_llm (the hand-copy had
  drifted: missing save_retriever_output); new fields_removed trait
  replaces schema.py's hardcoded op-type table

Rule/config plumbing:
- LimitPushdown removed from defaults (sound only under failure-free
  exact 1:1, which LLM ops cannot promise); opt in by name
- resolve_rules raises on unknown rule names and bad spec types,
  accepts a single string
- trigger_op_types pre-check skips the lift entirely when no rule
  could fire (runner-construction hot path)
- prepare_config: single-lift validate+rewrite used by MOAR; candidates
  now honor the root pipeline's plan_rewrites setting instead of
  unconditionally applying default rules
- runner gate falls back to the docetl.plan_rewrites module global
  (covers from_yaml/dict constructions); logs when a rewrite forces
  re-deriving a caller-passed Pipeline
- lower() preserves unknown keys in equijoin step entries
- read-after-removal demoted to warning (the extractor has known false
  positives on guarded templates; MOAR must not reject working plans)

Cleanup: shared _transparent_hop predicate (the two copies disagreed on
the shared-config check), dead node-family taxonomy and is_deterministic
trait removed, code-op traits deduplicated into a mixin, O(1) cached
consumer/reference lookups.

Adds regression tests for every confirmed exploit, including the two
verified end-to-end (input.get pushdown, bound-method pushdown).

* LimitPushdown joins the default rule set

Maintainer decision: the rule's exactness caveat (a silently dropped
LLM-timeout row shifts a downstream positional head's membership) only
manifests in runs the runtime is already corrupting via the silent
timeout-drop, so the rewrite adds no new failure mode. The caveat and
the per-pipeline escape hatch (plan_rewrites: ["selection_pushdown"])
stay documented on the rule; the fully sound scan-limit fusion remains
future work.

* Document plan rewrites; test Frame.plan()/explain()

Closes the two gaps a coverage audit found: the Frame plan surface had
no tests (plan() DAG shape, explain() rendering, optimized=True rule
listing, the docetl.plan_rewrites global, the schemas toggle), and the
default-ON rewrite behavior had no user-facing docs. New docs page
covers what the rules do, the fail-closed analysis, the limit-pushdown
caveat, per-pipeline and global opt-outs, the checkpoint-invalidation
note, and the MOAR integration (including DOCETL_MOAR_PLAN_SUMMARY).

* Derive blocking keys soundly; Frame.schema() delegates to the plan fold

Replaces four copy-pasted regex+split('.')[-1] heuristics (blocking.py,
resolve.py x2, join_optimizer.py) with one extract_comparison_field_reads
helper over the sound jinja extractor. The legacy heuristic missed reads
inside {% if %}/{% for %} blocks and mangled nested paths — for
input1.address.city it produced "city", a key the records don't have, so
blocking embedded empty strings for it. Roots are returned instead, and
unanalyzable (whole-row) prompts yield None, which every call site
already maps to its block-on-all-keys fallback. Resolve's output-key
mapping site gets the same treatment (its dotted paths could never match
a record key, silently nulling output fields).

Frame.schema() now delegates to the plan package's schema propagation —
one transform_schema fold instead of two, and equijoin frames get a real
left+right merge instead of a linear fold over the flat ops list.

* Simplify plan IR: merge 12 files → 6, delete graph_builder, unify renderers, add real MOAR e2e test

- Merge plan package: nodes.py+plan.py → ir.py, schema.py+validate.py → analysis.py,
  rules/pushdown.py → rewrite.py, inline prepare.py into __init__.py, delete explain.py
- Delete graph_builder.py: inline build_operation_graph into containers.py,
  compute_operation_hashes into runner.py
- Unify plan renderers: delete format_plan (plain-text), keep format_query_plan (Rich);
  add strip_markup() for MOAR agent prompts
- Runner now lifts config once and stores plan; syntax_check/list_pipeline_operations
  walk plan nodes instead of re-parsing config
- Add real end-to-end MOAR test with 3 models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini)

Net: -180 lines, 6 plan files instead of 12.

* Remove unnecessary lru_cache from code op field-read extractors

AST parsing a few-line transform is microseconds and runs once per
operation during plan lifting — caching adds complexity for no gain.
